I mean, most of the time, I don't check my phone every five minutes, and I usually have the sound turned off. Sometimes I just don't notice the messages, and other times I don't feel like responding immediately. I guess I don't want to feel obligated to pick up my phone every time it buzzes. If something is really important, people can call me, right? Otherwise, I'll respond when I feel like it. But then, my friend who was slightly drunk told me that I'm being a dick by doing this. He said that it barely takes any time to respond to most things and that not responding immediately implies that I don't care about others. I can see his point, but for me, it's more about the principle of the matter. I don't want to feel like I have to give people attention right away just because they send me a message. I want to have control over when and how I communicate. So, is it wrong to not respond to messages immediately? Or is it okay to set boundaries like this? I guess it depends on the situation and the people involved. If most people are fine with it, then maybe it's not a big deal. But if it's causing issues with some friends, then maybe I should reconsider my approach. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I can set some expectations with people about how quickly I'll respond, so they know what to expect. That way, it's not just me deciding when to respond, but we're on the same page about communication styles. Another thing to consider is the importance of the message. If it's something urgent, people can call me, as I mentioned before. But for less important things, taking a few hours to respond shouldn't be a problem, right? It's not like I'm ignoring them completely; I'm just not responding instantly. I also think about how technology has changed communication. We're so used to instant responses now, but that doesn't mean we have to respond instantly all the time. It's okay to take a break from constant connectivity. Plus, having the sound off and not checking my phone every five minutes helps me maintain a better work-life balance. But then, there's the argument that not responding immediately might make people feel like I don't care about them. I don't want that to happen. Maybe I should find a way to respond in a timely manner without feeling obligated to do so every single time. It's a bit of a balancing act. Overall, I think it's important to set boundaries for myself, but I also need to be considerate of others' feelings. If most people are okay with my approach, then it's probably fine. But if it's causing problems, I might need to adjust how I handle communication.
